timelines.title: Birth of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
timelines.description: Born as Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar in Mhow, Central Provinces (now Madhya Pradesh), to Ramji Maloji Sakpal and Bhimabai. He was the 14th child of the family.

timelines.title: Early Schooling — Satara
timelines.description: Family moved to Satara after father's transfer. Young Bhim attended local school, facing caste-based discrimination early in life.

timelines.title: Father Retired — Move to Bombay
timelines.description: Ramji Sakpal retired from military service. Family shifted to Bombay. Bhim enrolled at Elphinstone High School.

timelines.title: Matriculation — Elphinstone High School
timelines.description: Bhimrao passed matriculation from Elphinstone High School, Bombay. He was the first from his Mahar community to do so. Celebrated in his community.

timelines.title: Enrolled at Elphinstone College
timelines.description: Joined Elphinstone College, affiliated with University of Bombay. Studied Economics and Political Science.

timelines.title: Graduation — B.A. in Economics & Political Science
timelines.description: Graduated from Elphinstone College with a B.A. degree. His success was celebrated across the Mahar community. The degree was conferred by Bombay University.

timelines.title: Scholarship to Columbia University
timelines.description: Secured the Baroda State Scholarship of £11.50 per month for three years under the scheme of the Maharaja of Baroda. Left for New York to study at Columbia University.

timelines.title: M.A. — Columbia University
timelines.description: Completed M.A. in Economics at Columbia University. Specialized in Economics, Sociology, History, Philosophy and Anthropology. Thesis: 'Ancient Indian Commerce'.

timelines.title: Enrolled at London School of Economics
timelines.description: Enrolled at the London School of Economics. Began work on doctoral thesis. Also studied at Gray's Inn for law.

timelines.title: D.Sc. in Economics — LSE
timelines.description: Completed his second doctorate — D.Sc. in Economics from LSE. His thesis 'The Problem of the Rupee' examined currency systems and gold exchange standards.

timelines.title: Called to the Bar — Gray's Inn
timelines.description: Qualified as a barrister-at-law from Gray's Inn, London. Returned to India in 1923 with multiple advanced degrees — an extraordinary achievement for someone from his community.

timelines.title: Started Legal Practice in Bombay
timelines.description: Established his legal practice in Bombay High Court. Also taught at the prestigious Sydenham College of Commerce.

timelines.title: Appointed to Bombay University Senate
timelines.description: Nominated to the Senate of Bombay University. Began working on social reform for the depressed classes.

timelines.title: Called for Separate Electorates — Simon Commission
timelines.description: Appeared before the Simon Commission and demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes. This became a key point in constitutional negotiations.

timelines.title: First Round Table Conference
timelines.description: Participated in the First Round Table Conference in London as a representative of the Depressed Classes. Demanded separate electorates for untouchables.

timelines.title: Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi
timelines.description: Negotiated the Poona Pact with Gandhi. Agreed to abandon separate electorates in exchange for reserved seats within the general electorate. 18% reservation for Depressed Classes in legislatures guaranteed.

timelines.title: Second Round Table Conference
timelines.description: Participated in the Second Round Table Conference. Continued advocacy for Depressed Classes rights.

timelines.title: Published 'Annihilation of Caste'
timelines.description: Self-published 'Annihilation of Caste' after the original organizers cancelled his speech. Over 15,000 copies sold. Considered one of the most important critiques of caste ever written.

timelines.title: Founded Independent Labour Party
timelines.description: Founded the Independent Labour Party (ILP) in Bombay. The party contested elections and won several seats, marking Ambedkar's entry into electoral politics.

timelines.title: Bombay Legislative Council — Elected Member
timelines.description: Elected to the Bombay Legislative Council as an Independent Labour Party candidate. Became Leader of the Opposition.

timelines.title: Appointed to Viceroy's Executive Council
timelines.description: Nominated to the Viceroy's Executive Council as Labour Member. Worked on labor rights, minimum wages, and working conditions for industrial workers.

timelines.title: Elected to Constituent Assembly
timelines.description: Elected to the Constituent Assembly of India from Bengal (as a representative of the Depressed Classes). Would become the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

timelines.title: Appointed First Law Minister of India
timelines.description: Appointed as the first Law Minister of independent India by Prime Minister Nehru. Also served as Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

timelines.title: Constitution Adopted
timelines.description: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949. Ambedkar moved the motion: 'The Constitution is passed.'

timelines.title: Resigned from Cabinet — Hindu Code Bill
timelines.description: Resigned from Nehru's cabinet due to disagreement over the Hindu Code Bill. Felt the bill was being diluted.

timelines.title: Elected to Lok Sabha — Bombay North
timelines.description: Contested the first general election from Bombay North (Central) constituency and won. Became a member of the First Lok Sabha.

timelines.title: Published 'Buddha and His Dhamma'
timelines.description: Published 'Buddha and His Dhamma', his final major work. Presented Buddhism as a rational, scientific philosophy.

timelines.title: Embraced Buddhism — Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur
timelines.description: On October 14, 1956, at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur, Ambedkar formally embraced Buddhism along with approximately 500,000 followers — the largest mass conversion in history.

timelines.title: Passing of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
timelines.description: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar passed away in his sleep at his Delhi residence on December 6, 1956. He was 65. Cremated at Dadar Chowpatty, Mumbai, per Buddhist rites. Millions attended.
